message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and overall importance:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and the Pacific; one of the busiest airports on the West Coast. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the oldest major hubs; key connecting point for domestic and international flights. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City | New York | JFK | Major international gateway; primary hub for many carriers including Delta and JetBlue. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco | California | SFO | Key hub for transpacific flights; major hub for United Airlines. |
| Seattle‑Tacoma International Airport | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for other carriers. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for Latin American and Caribbean traffic; key hub for American Airlines. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix | Arizona | PHX | Major hub for Southwest Airlines; high passenger volume. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport | Charlotte | North Carolina | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports. |
| Orlando International Airport | Orlando | Florida | MCO | Major hub for leisure travel; key hub for Southwest Airlines. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport | Newark | New Jersey | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; important for East Coast traffic. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport | Washington, D.C. | Virginia | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; key for government and diplomatic travel. |

These airports are among the busiest in the country and serve as major hubs for both domestic and international flights.
